newsitem.title: USA: HemaSure sees better LeukoNet filter sales.
newsitem.headline: HemaSure sees better LeukoNet filter sales.

text.p: HemaSure Inc President and Chief Executive Officer Steven Rouhander said he expects sales of the company's LeukoNet blood filter to improve this year, after falling short of expectations in 1996.

"It was tougher than we had thought to penetrate this market," Rouhander said of the filter, which removes harmful leukocytes from blood supplies. "However, once you do get customers to switch, they stay with you."

Speaking at the Hambrecht and Quist healthcare conference here, Rouhander said part of the disappointment in 1996 sales was due to the company's agreement to improve its standard for the filter before it completed contracts with major customers.

He said the attention to quality helped it secure major contracts with the American Red Cross, Blood Centers of America and several similar international organizations. HemaSure has a three-year, $50 million purchase agreement for the filters with the American Red Cross.

"Our decision to improve the filter was not looked upon favorably by the Street, but it was important in terms of our long-term position. I think 1997 is the year when investors will be rewarded for their patience in 1996."
Rouhander also told the conference HemaSure will seek premarket approval in about a year of its Steripath blood purification system.
